stem:
Tushar measures a ribbon using the fractional unit $\dfrac{1}{6}$ metre. Exactly $11$ of those units cover the ribbon end to end.

Which claim correctly writes the ribbon length?

options.text: The ribbon length is $\dfrac{11}{6}$ metres even if a different whole is used for the unit $\dfrac{1}{6}$.
The count $11$ produces the unit $\dfrac{1}{6}$, so start from $11$ and invent the fractional unit afterward.
The ribbon length is $11.6$ metres, by reading the digits as a decimal conversion.

teacher.key_rationale: Eleven copies of 1/6 metre make 11/6 metres when the unit whole is fixed. Dropping the fixed-whole condition, reversing so the count invents the unit, or treating the digits as a decimal conversion miss the hinge.
